about: The communio of the formulary “Blessed Virgin Mary of the Rosary” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Put forth blossoms like the lily, give forth fragrance and put forth lovely leaves; sing a song of praise and bless the Lord in His works.

ex.w002: Flores names what is produced: blossoms. As an internal object of florete, the phrase means “put forth blossoms”. The form could also be vocative, but the object reading better fits this image.
ex.w011: Gratia here denotes beauty or charm. The whole phrase depicts the plant putting forth lovely leaves.
ex.w012: The song expresses praise offered to God. The phrase is therefore rendered “sing a song of praise”, not an invitation to praise the song itself.
ex.w019: The possessive refers to the Lord: these are His works, not the works of the people addressed by the command.
